NORML Analysis of Federal Appeals Court Ruling On Medical Marijuana Clubs
-- NORML Weekly PR

(MarijuanaNews note: This is very important! This ruling allows members of the Oakland CBC – and other clubs – to argue that they have a fundamental right to use medical marijuana.

The 9th Circuit covers the western DEAland states, all of which have medical marijuana laws, so this ruling has an immediate practical impact. When the Feds asked the full 9th Circuit to review the previous favorable rulings by the 3 judge panel, they refused, thereby upholding the rulings. This will end up at the Supreme Court in a few years, but not before greatly complicating things for the feds.

This ruling would appear to have relevance for the McCormick and McWilliams cases, and many others.)

See
Judge Rules Against Medical Necessity Defense For McCormick and McWilliams
There Cannot Be Even a Mention of Medical Marijuana! Defies 9th Circuit Ruling.
Press Release From McCormick and McWilliams

May 12, 2000
Circuit Rules in Favor of Pot Users
By Jason Hoppin
From http://www.callaw.com/stories/edt0512m.html

Medical marijuana users won a court victory Wednesday when the Ninth Circuit U.S. Court of Appeals reinstated a defense tossed out by a lower court judge.

The three-judge ruling allows users to argue before U.S. District Judge Charles Breyer that their pot-smoking is a fundamental right, a defense Breyer ruled was inadmissible in court.

The victory was foreshadowed by an Oakland medical marijuana club's win last year in United States v. Oakland Cannabis Buyer's Cooperative, 190 F. 3d 1109. Breyer ruled in favor of the government's suit to shut down the pot club, but his decision was overturned by the same panel of appellate judges, Judges Stephen Reinhardt, Mary Schroeder and Barry Silverman.

The Ninth Circuit's May 10 order will give several club patrons another opportunity to argue in favor of medical marijuana use in the Oakland Cannabis litigation.

" The district court entered its order of dismissal underlying this appeal before we decided the earlier appeal. Accordingly, we vacate the district court's order and remand for consideration in light of our prior opinion, " read the unpublished opinion.

Breyer will now have to allow club members to put up a defense that smoking marijuana to alleviate ailments is a fundamental right. Reinhardt addressed the point in a separate concurrence.

" I would suggest ... the district judge consider whether the constitutional claim should be resolved on summary judgement, rather than on a motion to dismiss, given the Supreme Court's emphasis on examining, in substantive due process cases, a claimed right's basis in 'our nation's history, legal traditions and practices.' "

The case is Unites States v. Oakland Cannabis Buyer's Cooperative, 99-15838.
